newsitem.title: FRANCE: Hippos lose teeth to meet Far East ivory demand.
newsitem.headline: Hippos lose teeth to meet Far East ivory demand.

text.p: French customs have seized more than 1,700 hippopotamus teeth from smugglers apparently diversifying away from elephant tusks to meet demand for ivory in the Far East.

The load of 1,738 hippopotamus teeth, one elephant tusk and four wart-hog teeth was seized at Paris' Orly airport last month en route from Uganda to Hong-Kong, the customs service said in a statement on Thursday. All are protected species.
"The persistence of demand for ivory in the Far East is leading traffickers to find species other than elephants, especially hippotamuses, to satisfy this demand," it said.
